item.title: Blue Origin seeking to increase New Glenn launch cadence at Cape Canaveral
item.description: As Blue Origin continues to recover from a New Glenn pad explosion in May, the company is seeking permission to significantly increase the vehicle’s launch rate.

item.title: FCC votes to exclude space from NEPA reviews
item.description: The FCC voted Sept. 30 to formally exclude the space activities it regulates from reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act, while also making more than 1,000 megahertz of spectrum available for the industry.

item.title: Chinese electric-pump rocket startup Z-Trak raises new funding, targets 2027 debut for reusable Fission-A
item.description: HELSINKI — Chinese launch startup Z-Trak Space has secured a new funding round for a small reusable rocket and is targeting late 2027 for a first flight.

item.title: Viridian wins NASA contract to explore aerodynamic control surfaces for VLEO operations
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO – Viridian Space will work with the University of Washington to improve the simulation and design of control surfaces for satellites maneuvering in very low Earth orbit (VLEO), under a $225,000 NASA Small Business Technology Transfer contract announced Sept. 30.

item.description: Varda Space Industries, a company that operates reentry spacecraft for pharmaceutical and hypersonics research applications, has raised $251 million as it prepares to launch three missions in the next month.

item.description: SAN FRANCISCO — Sophia Space and Redwire Corp. announced an agreement Sept. 30 to work together to address development and deployment of scalable, space-based computing infrastructure.

item.description: HELSINKI — Chinese commercial launch firm CAS Space is targeting a first flight of the Lihong-2 suborbital rocket in early 2027, carrying pharmaceutical payloads.

item.title: Blackswan raises $2.9 million seed round for satellite rendezvous technology
item.description: Lithuania’s Blackswan Space has raised around $2.9 million to support the development of its rendezvous & proximity operations payload, which Orbit Fab plans to use for Europe’s first in-space refueling demo in 2028.

item.title: AstroForge to test full spacecraft autonomy using AI
item.description: Space mining company AstroForge plans to fly a spacecraft next year that will test its ability to operate fully autonomously using artificial intelligence.
